step by step, in plain words

• A2DP (music profile) is stereo output only; its microphone needs the hands-free profile (HFP), which Windows exposes as a separate mono 'Hands-Free' endpoint and drops the output to phone quality while it is open.
• Latency 100-250 ms from the codec (SBC / AAC / aptX): monitoring a stream or playback is fine, playing an instrument live is not.
• DirectSound has no exclusive lock: Windows keeps mixing other programs into the device. ASIO never sees Bluetooth.
• Blocks under 256 frames gain nothing here; 512 is a good start.

From the last sweep. The delay is the acoustic path (loopback: the round-trip latency); APPLY sets it as the strip delay for time alignment. RT60 needs a decay of 25 dB (T20) or 35 dB (T30) above the noise: a quiet room and a loud sweep.

A rectangular room with rigid walls: the mode frequencies are exact for that shape, the response is a prediction (modal sum with the damping of the RT60). Move the speaker and the listener to see which modes each place excites; real rooms differ, so confirm with a sweep.

Peaking filters fitted to the last measured response inside the range (20 - 400 Hz by default: the range where a room, not the speaker, sets the response).
